key_insight: Interface orientation tunes thermal transport in lateral MoSe₂/MoS₂ heterostructures: extrapolated infinite-length conductance is 473 MW/m²K for armchair versus 387 MW/m²K for zigzag interfaces.
engineering_relevance: Choosing armchair interfaces could improve heat dissipation in lateral TMD nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices.
method: Train a deep learning interatomic potential with DeePMD-kit using DFT data.
Run non-equilibrium molecular dynamics for armchair and zigzag interfaces over 10–40 nm cell lengths.
Extrapolate conductance to infinite length and analyze temperature dependence and vibrational spectra.
evidence_signal: The potential closely reproduces DFT energies, forces, and phonon dispersions; armchair conductance is higher at every tested length and shows greater phonon spectral overlap at 300 K.
watch_item: The reported conductances are simulation-based extrapolations; experimental validation and sensitivity to interface defects remain to be established.
paper_title: Orientation-Tunable Interfacial Thermal Conductance in Lateral MoSe2/MoS2 Heterostructures: A Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
